answers.answer: Shuffle all four Conflict III cards and put them at the bottom; shuffle the nine Conflict II cards and deal five on top; shuffle the three Conflict I cards and deal one on top. The resulting 10-card deck has one I, five II, and four III. Return unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup, Create the Conflict Deck: 'Shuffle the four Conflict III cards' ... 'deal five' Conflict II and 'deal one' Conflict I; 'Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.'

answers.answer: A human starts at 1 VP in a four-player game and 0 VP in a three-player game. In either game, the human has two Agents on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; starts with three troops in their garrison and the remaining nine in supply; and takes 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup: Score track is 'on the 1 space in a 4-player game, otherwise on the 0 space'; two Agents go on the Leader and the Swordmaster beside the board; place 'three' troops in a garrison and the 'remaining nine' in supply; 'Take 1 water.'

answers.answer: Yes. You may take a Reveal turn while Agents remain. After taking it, your turns are skipped for the rest of that phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come from the Reveal boxes of cards revealed from the remaining hand, not cards already played on Agent turns. During Clean Up, all cards in front of you from both Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: 'Agent turns are optional; you may take a Reveal turn while you still have Agents' and after it 'your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.' Reveal Turn: resolve 'just-revealed cards only (not ... cards played on Agent turns)'; Clean Up moves 'all cards in front of you ... to your discard pile.'

answers.answer: No. Costs must be paid immediately before resolving effects of the space or the card played, so that card's Agent-box effect cannot fund entry. One card sends only one Agent, using one Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be played on an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs 'immediately (before resolving any effects of the space or the card you played)'; 'You choose only one Agent icon; one card can't send multiple Agents'; 'A card with no Agent icons can't be played on an Agent turn.'

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy the three troops recruited this turn plus up to two of the four already in your garrison, for at most five troops. At a non-Combat destination you deploy none. Recruited troops are taken from your supply and placed in your garrison; at a Combat space, troops recruited during the current turn may then be deployed.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying Units: recruit a troop 'from your supply' into the garrison. At a Combat space deploy 'any or all units recruited during your current turn ... plus up to two more units from your garrison.'

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any board space connected to an observation post where you have a Spy; this does not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to enter a space occupied by another player's Agent. Gather Intelligence can be chosen whenever you send an Agent: recall a connected Spy to draw a card, deciding immediately after placing the Agent and before receiving space or card effects. The same Spy cannot be used for both effects, though two different Spies can be used on the same placement for one Infiltrate and one Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Spies & observation posts: Spy icon sends to a space connected to a post where you have a Spy and 'you do not recall the Spy'; Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence recall a Spy, and 'You cannot recall the same Spy to both' (though one of each is possible using different Spies). Gather Intelligence is decided after placement, before effects.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops contribute 4, one sandworm contributes 3, and four revealed swords contribute 4. If your final unit is removed, strength becomes 0; swords alone do not give strength without a unit in the Conflict. You cannot participate in Combat Intrigue with no unit, because only players with at least one unit in the Conflict may play it.
answers.evidence: Strength: each troop is 2, each sandworm 3, each revealed sword 1; you must have 'at least one unit in the Conflict'; if the last unit is removed, strength is 0. Combat begins with eligible players having 'at least one unit in the Conflict.'

answers.answer: Yes. Passing once does not prevent you from playing another Combat Intrigue if an opponent later plays one. The window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply and sandworms to the bank.
answers.evidence: Combat: players may play Combat Intrigue or pass; 'You are not required to pass just because you passed earlier'; resolve once all involved pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to 'supply' and sandworms to the 'bank.'

answers.answer: In a four-player Conflict, two players tied for first each get the second reward; neither wins or takes the Conflict card. The remaining players compete for the third reward. In a three-player Conflict, the tied players each get the second reward and no other rewards are given; neither takes the Conflict card. A player with zero strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties: tied first players 'each gain the second reward' and 'no one wins ... or takes the Conflict card.' With three or fewer players, no other rewards; with four, exactly two tied leaves others to compete for third. Resolve Combat: a player with '0 strength receives no reward.'

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double a reward once; two sandworms do not quadruple it. Taking control of a location and battle icons on won Conflict cards cannot be doubled. For a reward offering 3 spice for 1 VP, the doubled reward lets you pay 3 spice for 1 VP or pay 6 spice for 2 VP (if you choose to pay).
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: 'if you have one or more sandworms ... double the rewards'; control and battle icons cannot be doubled. For optional-cost rewards, 'you may pay the cost a second time'; example allows 3 spice for 1 VP or 6 for 2.

answers.answer: After winning and taking the Conflict card into your supply, check it against your other face-up Conflict or Objective cards for a matching battle icon. If there is a match, you must flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, the wild icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply, also flipping the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Battle Icons: when you win and take the card into your supply, check for another 'face-up Conflict or Objective card' with the same icon; if present, 'must flip the matching pair face down and gain 1 VP.' During Endgame, wild may match any of the three.

answers.answer: Reaching 2 Influence gives 1 VP; that VP is lost below 2 and regained on reaching 2 again. Reaching 4 gives the printed track bonus; it is kept if Influence drops below 4 and earned again when you climb back to 4. The first player to reach 4 gets the Alliance token and its 1 VP. Tying the current holder at 4 does not take the Alliance.
answers.evidence: Influence scoring table: Reach 2 gives 1 VP, lost below 2 and regained at 2; Reach 4 gives the printed bonus, kept below 4 and earned again on return; 'Tying the current holder does not steal it.'

answers.answer: You may spend Persuasion before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from multiple sources to buy one card and split Persuasion from one source among different cards. The Row is replenished to five cards after a purchase, and you may immediately buy the replacement if you can afford it. An acquired card goes face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Reveal Effects: Persuasion may be used 'before, between, or after' effects. Acquiring Cards: Persuasion may be pooled or split; the Row must always have five cards, so you may acquire a replacement; acquired cards go face up into the discard pile.

answers.answer: During Makers, each Maker space without an Agent gets 1 bonus spice; when you later send an Agent to a Maker space, you gain all bonus spice there. At Deep Desert or Hagga Basin, you may take the base spice or, if you have Maker Hooks, summon respectively two or one sandworms. Hooks are acquired at Sietch Tabr if you lack them, are retained rather than spent, and are not a universal prerequisite when an effect does not specify them. The Shield Wall prevents summoning at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while it remains on the board. A sandworm is placed directly in your Conflict quadrant; it can never go in a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers: each empty Maker space gets 1 spice; an Agent gains all bonus spice there. Board Space Guide: Deep Desert chooses 4 spice or, with Hooks, two worms; Hagga chooses 2 spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Sandworms: Hooks are not spent; worms are immediately deployed to the Conflict and can never be placed in a garrison; Shield Wall protection applies to the three named locations.

answers.answer: At the end of a round, reaching at least 10 VP or having an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue cards; then the player with the most VP wins. A tie is broken by spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: 'At the end of a round' with 10+ VP or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame; first resolve Endgame Intrigue, then compare VP. Tiebreakers: spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops.

answers.answer: Standard CHOAM setup has two contracts face up and the remaining 18 of the 20 standard contracts face down in the bank. Add four Intrigue cards and four Imperium cards. Shaddam Corrino IV is an optional Leader choice, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay in the box and are not part of standard CHOAM setup.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes: shuffle 20, flip two face up, place remaining 18 face down; add 4 Intrigue and 4 Imperium cards; Shaddam is 'an option.' Components/scope: the 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix; leave them in the box for standard CHOAM.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, a contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it with a face-up contract from the bank. If all contracts have been taken by players, the icon instead gives 2 Solari. Complete a Harvest contract by sending an Agent to a Maker space and gaining the specified total spice during that turn, including other sources. Complete the Immediate contract as soon as you take it. Complete the Acquire The Spice Must Flow contract when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts: take a face-up contract and replace it from the bank; if all are taken, the icon gives 2 Solari. Completing contracts defines Harvest, Immediate, and Acquire The Spice Must Flow completion conditions.

answers.answer: No. You must have held the contract when you sent the Agent, so one gained afterward waits until a future turn. When you complete it, announce completion, gain the shown rewards, then flip the contract face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: if you take a contract for a space where you 'already sent your Agent this turn,' you must wait; you must have held it when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain rewards, and flip it face down, leaving it in your supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. The Rival receives the Ornithopter Objective. The human whose Objective shows the First Player marker takes First Player; it alternates only between the humans. Turn order is First Player, then Rival, then the other human. The Rival takes Agent turns while an Agent remains in supply and never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: 'one shared scoring Rival'; give it Ornithopter, and First Player goes to the human whose card shows it. First Player alternates only between humans; turn order is First Player → Rival → other human. Rival 'never takes a Reveal turn.'

answers.answer: When Hagal indicates an occupied destination, ignore it and reveal again. A Place Spy card places a Spy at an empty post of its specified type (or ignores the placement if none is available), then reveals another Hagal card because it has not sent an Agent. The Rival ignores ordinary board-space costs and effects, applying only the Hagal card effects. If House Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle it and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: 'Ignore an occupied destination and reveal again.' Spies and Schemes: Place Spy uses an empty post of the specified type or ignores placement if none, and reveals another card because it has not sent an Agent. Rival ignores normal space costs/effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, reshuffle immediately and continue.
